# Implementation Plan: Crews Protocol v3.0.0 Envelope Field Renames

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-05-31. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/crews-protocol-v200-envelope-renames/plan.md`.*

*This is v2 of the plan, amended after a three-reviewer pass (Claude / Codex / Copilot). The v1 draft is preserved at `<staging>/draft-plan.v1.md`. Key amendments are summarized in the changelog at the bottom of this file.*

## Overview

Two breaking-change envelope-field renames bundled into a single atomic
crews-plugin **v3.0.0** ship (baseline is v2.4.1 per
`.claude-plugin/plugin.json:4` and the marketplace entries — v1 of this
plan said 2.4.0):

- **Rename A** — `row.from.kind` (and `env.from.kind`) → `row.from.routingKind`
  (and `env.from.routingKind`). Disambiguates the routing-identity field on
  inbox-history / mailbox / system-mailbox rows from the *report kind*
  emitted by members (`row.kind` ∈ `progress|done|question|blocked`). The
  collision between `row.kind` (report content) and `row.from.kind`
  (routing reason) has already caused confusion during v2.3.0 work.

- **Rename B** — `payload.replyToId` → `payload.replyTo`. Eliminates the
  asymmetry with the outbox/envelope top-level `replyTo` field, which is
  documented in the v2.3.0 CHANGELOG as intentional but creates friction
  every time someone hand-writes a fixture.

The follow-on `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan` job will execute the
renames in a single PR/commit across schema, factories, the
`appendSystemMailbox` chokepoint, the direct payload-setting call sites,
every consumer, every test fixture, every assertion, every documentation
page, every version-stamp file, and a new explicit-rejection ruleset in
the schema validator. Gated by the v2.3.2 producer/consumer enforcement
test extended with positive-and-negative assertions plus a new
strict-mode validator-rejection suite.

**Schema location (the single in-process chokepoint).**
`D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/hooks/protocol/envelope.js`:

- `kindEnum` (lines 45–61): the *routing-kind enum* shared between
  `env.kind` (report kind) and `env.from.kind` (routing kind). The
  comment at line 40 explicitly notes one enum covers both axes.
  After rename, only the field name moves; the enum stays shared.
- `PAYLOAD_RULES` (lines 72–101): per-routing-kind required-payload
  contract. `member-reply` requires `replyToId: 'string'` at line 75 —
  the Field B canonical declaration. **Today PAYLOAD_RULES has only
  `required`, no `forbidden` clause** — see "Schema rejection
  semantics" below; v3.0.0 must add `forbidden` to lock the rename in.
- `CANONICAL_ADDRESSES` (lines 105–112): introspectable registry
  consumed by `canonicalAddressFor()`. Currently has `'from.kind':
  'env.from.kind'` (line 110) and `'payload.replyToId':
  'env.payload.replyToId'` (line 111).
- `validateFromSubfields()` (lines 144–161): validates `from.role` /
  `from.kind` / `from.name` / `from.crew` / `from.triggeredBy`. **Does
  NOT reject unknown `from.*` subfields today** — a row with the
  legacy `from.kind` after rename would pass the validator unchanged
  unless v3.0.0 adds an explicit blacklist. This is a key amendment
  vs the v1 draft.
- `validatePayloadRules()` (lines 170–187): per-kind dispatch reads
  `env.from.kind` at line 171 into a local variable already named
  `routingKind` — the new field name aligns with existing in-code
  terminology, which is one reason `routingKind` is the right choice.
- `validateEnvelope()` (lines 210–228) and `validateOutboxRow()` (lines
  230–246) both delegate `from.*` validation to `validateFromSubfields()`.
- Module-level CANONICAL ADDRESS CONTRACT comment block (lines 3–35)
  documents both fields with rationale, including the "SEPARATE ADDRESS
  … kept at its current address" note for `payload.replyToId` — which
  is exactly what v3.0.0 reverses.
- `buildEnvelope()` (lines 254–270) and `buildOutboxRow()` (lines
  278–299) are the producer factories. Their signatures accept
  arbitrary `from` / `payload` shapes; **no factory-signature change
  is required**.

**Central producer chokepoint (this was MISSED in v1).**
`D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/hooks/mailbox.js:501–531`
— `appendSystemMailbox(name, crew, cwd, messageOrEnvelope, opts)`:

- Line 503–507: builds the `from` field as
  `{ role: 'system', kind: opts.kind || 'thread-fanout', triggeredBy: ... }`.
- Line 526: passes the same shape to `buildEnvelope({ ..., from: { role,
  kind: opts.kind || null, triggeredBy, name, crew }, ... })`.
- **This is the canonical producer for Field A.** Every system-mailbox
  caller (`threads.fanoutThreadNotifications`, member-reply notify in
  stop.js, member-question routing in pre-tool-use, etc.) passes a
  routing kind via `opts.kind`, and this function writes it into the
  envelope as `from.kind`. After rename, BOTH locations (line 505 AND
  line 526) write `from.routingKind` instead. Callers do not need to
  change — `opts.kind` is the caller-facing API name (a routing intent)
  and stays the same; the **wire-shape** field name on `from.*` is
  what changes.

**Direct producer of `payload.replyToId` (Field B).**
`D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/hooks/stop.js:1077–1089` — the
member-reply notify call site sets `payload: { ..., replyToId:
row.replyTo, ... }` at line 1085 and also `kind: 'member-reply'` in
`opts` at line 1089. The `replyToId` key is set inline in the payload
object literal here and must be renamed to `replyTo`. (The `kind:
'member-reply'` opts value is the routing intent — it stays unchanged
because it's the caller-facing API; `appendSystemMailbox` is what
writes it into `from.routingKind` on the wire.)

### Technical Constraints

- **`CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA=1` is the test-runner default (v2.4.0+).**
  Schema, factories, the chokepoint, direct producers, every consumer,
  every fixture, every version file, and every doc page MUST land in
  the same commit/PR. A staged approach (schema first, code later)
  cannot work because CI hard-fails at the seam.

- **Schema rejection semantics today are LAX, not strict.** Two
  important nuances missed in v1:
  1. `validateFromSubfields()` validates *known* `from.*` subfield
     types but does NOT reject *unknown* subfields. After rename, a
     stale row carrying `from.kind` would pass validation as an
     "extra" subfield. v3.0.0 must explicitly reject `from.kind`
     (and other renamed legacy names) in `validateFromSubfields` to
     guarantee the rename sticks.
  2. `PAYLOAD_RULES` rules currently only have a `required` clause,
     no `forbidden`. After rename, a stale row with `payload.replyToId`
     would pass alongside the new `payload.replyTo`. v3.0.0 must
     add `forbidden: { replyToId: true }` to
     `PAYLOAD_RULES['member-reply']` (and extend
     `validatePayloadRules` to honour it). This is a small additive
     schema feature, not a new validator pattern.

- **Production stays warn-only** via `schema-warning:` log lines.
  Existing v2.4.x behaviour is preserved: a real user on v3.0.0 with a
  stale consumer gets a warning, not a crash. CI is the strict-mode
  gate.

- **The schema is *code*, not JSON Schema.** All five primitives
  (`kindEnum`, `PAYLOAD_RULES`, `CANONICAL_ADDRESSES`,
  `validateFromSubfields`, `validatePayloadRules`) live in the same
  file (`hooks/protocol/envelope.js`) and must be edited together.

- **On-disk JSONL legacy (mid-flight upgrade).** Inbox-history rows
  are persisted at `.crews/<crew>/inbox/<actor>/history.jsonl` (read
  via `readInboxHistorySince` in `hooks/mailbox.js` and surfaced by
  `hooks/commands/review-mail.js:193`). Pre-upgrade rows on disk carry
  `from.kind` / `payload.replyToId` and would be misread by v3.0.0
  consumers. See "Mid-flight upgrade" in Risks for the policy
  decision (no read-side migration; operator restart required).

- **No external (out-of-tree) consumers identified.** Marketplace
  consumers install via `copilot plugin update` against `@latest`, so
  an alias period offers zero protection — they receive v3.0.0 whole.
  Internal consumer count: 70 `from.kind` matches + 36 `replyToId`
  matches in the crews plugin; 7 + 8 doc/task-text matches in codexu
  (non-runtime). Zero matches in any other plugin under
  `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/`.

## Approach

### Architecture

**Atomic, bundled, single-PR rename** with explicit schema rejection
of the old names plus a one-line operator-upgrade caveat for stale
on-disk JSONL. No deprecated-alias period. No consumer-side
read-migration shim.

The rename mechanics are simple — both fields are accessed via direct
property access in every grep hit; no dynamic / computed access exists.
The amendment vs v1: add new `forbidden`-clause schema rules so a
silent regression (a later producer reintroducing the old name) is
caught at the validator gate, not just at producer-fixture assertion
time.

### Implementation Strategy

The follow-on `/implement-with-ralph` job decomposes into 6 user
stories that all land in the same PR (no story is independently
shippable; the boundary is for review/parallelism convenience).

1. **US-001 — Schema rename + new rejection rules.**
   `hooks/protocol/envelope.js` only:
   - Rename in comments (lines 3–35) — drop the "kept at its current
     address" note for `payload.replyToId`.
   - Update `PAYLOAD_RULES['member-reply'].required.replyToId` → `.replyTo`.
   - Add `PAYLOAD_RULES['member-reply'].forbidden = { replyToId: true }`
     (new feature in the schema) and extend `validatePayloadRules` to
     honour it.
   - Update `CANONICAL_ADDRESSES`: drop `'from.kind'` and
     `'payload.replyToId'`; add `'from.routingKind'` and `'payload.replyTo'`.
   - Update `validateFromSubfields`: rename the `from.kind` validation
     to `from.routingKind`, AND add an explicit rejection: if `from.kind`
     is present (legacy name), call `fail()` with a clear message
     mentioning the rename. Symmetric for any other renamed `from.*`
     subfields (only `kind` today).
   - Update `validatePayloadRules` (line 171) to read
     `env.from.routingKind` instead of `env.from.kind`.
   - Update the `kindEnum` comment at line 40 ("from.routingKind
     routing values" instead of "from.kind routing values").

2. **US-002 — Producer chokepoint + direct payload setters.**
   - `hooks/mailbox.js` — `appendSystemMailbox()` at lines 501–531:
     change the field name written into `from.kind` (lines 505 AND
     526) to `from.routingKind`. **Caller signatures unchanged.**
   - `hooks/stop.js:1085` — member-reply notify call site: rename
     `replyToId: row.replyTo` to `replyTo: row.replyTo` in the inline
     payload object.

3. **US-003 — Non-test consumer rename.**
   - `hooks/protocol/review-required.js:14` — `envelope.from.kind` →
     `envelope.from.routingKind`.
   - `hooks/commands/review-mail.js:84–88` — `rowKind()` fallback:

   - `hooks/stop.js:208–209` — `entry.from.kind` →

   - `hooks/stop.js:265` — `entry.from.kind === 'member-question-request'`
     → `entry.from.routingKind === 'member-question-request'`.

4. **US-004 — Test + fixture migration (producer-path matrix).**
   Update every test file in "Test surface" above (~ 32 files) to
   produce and assert the new field shape. The
   `tests/protocol-envelope-enforcement.test.js` matrix gets BOTH
   positive (new shape written) AND negative (old name absent from

   `from.routingKind`. For `payload.replyTo`, negative assertions are

5. **US-005 — Validator strict-rejection tests.** New unit tests in

6. **US-006 — Documentation + CHANGELOG + version bump.**

## Scope

### In Scope

- Atomic rename of `from.kind` → `from.routingKind` everywhere.
- Atomic rename of `payload.replyToId` → `payload.replyTo` everywhere.
- New schema-level rejection rules (`validateFromSubfields` rejects
  `from.kind`; `PAYLOAD_RULES` gains a `forbidden` clause and
  `validatePayloadRules` honours it).
- Validator strict-rejection tests as a new unit-test bloc.
- Documentation + CHANGELOG + plugin version bump 2.4.1 → 3.0.0 across
  ALL version-stamp files (5 + the test literal).

### Out of Scope

- Read-side legacy fallback for stale on-disk JSONL rows (operator
  restart is the documented migration; see Risks).
- Deprecated-alias period or dual-emit transitional code.
- Any rename of the top-level `replyTo` (which is the *target* of
  Rename B, not a separate change).
- Any change to `row.kind` / `env.kind` / the report-kind enum
  (`progress|done|question|blocked|...`) — only the *routing* field on
  `from.*` is touched. The shared `kindEnum` value list is unchanged;
  only its location-name in the `from.*` object changes.
- Any change to other plugins (`ralph`, `ralph-overview`, etc.) —
  research confirmed zero consumer matches.
- Retroactive rewrite of codexu historical bookkeeping artifacts or of
  pre-v3.0.0 CHANGELOG entries.
- Mixed-version coexistence support (v2.4.x and v3.0.0 crews in the
  same workspace is unsupported; documented in CHANGELOG and
  implicitly enforced by the marketplace single-version pin).

## Risk Areas

1. **Test fixture sprawl (~33 test files).** Mechanical rename in a
   long list of test files. Risk: a missed fixture passes production
   code but silently uses the old name. Mitigation: US-005's
   strict-rejection tests + US-001's `validateFromSubfields` blacklist
   means a missed fixture trips the validator throw under
   `CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA=1` (the CI default). Plus the implementer's
   final pre-commit grep.

2. **Version file sprawl (5 + 1 files).** `version.test.js` enforces
   that all 5 stamp files plus its own literal carry the same string.
   Forgetting any one fails CI. Mitigation: US-006 enumerates all 6
   files explicitly; implementer can write a one-liner that bumps all
   with a single sed/`jq` pass.

3. **Subprocess hooks not visible to in-process matrix test.** The
   v2.3.2 enforcement test monkey-patches the in-process require-cache
   and cannot see subprocess-driven hooks (`stop.js`, `pre-tool-use.js`).
   Mitigation: those hooks are covered transitively by hook tests run
   under `CREWS_STRICT_ENVELOPE=1` (also default in v2.4.x); the
   pretooluse-ask-user-question and stop-member-* tests in US-004
   exercise them; the new US-005 strict-rejection bloc explicitly
   feeds malformed shapes to the validator.

4. **Manifest persistence of routing fields.** Codex research did NOT
   find `from.kind` / `payload.replyToId` persisted in manifest state
   files. **Implementer preflight (mandatory)**: grep
   `.crews/manifest*` fixture shapes AND `hooks/manifest*.js` / any
   manifest-reading helper for the legacy field names before US-001.
   If any hit appears, surface as a story-blocker and add a manifest
   migration story BEFORE merging. Manifest-test surface to inspect:
   `tests/protocol-manifest.test.js` (separate file, not in main
   rename scope).

5. **Mid-flight upgrade / on-disk JSONL legacy.** When a workspace
   upgrades from v2.4.1 → v3.0.0, existing `.crews/<crew>/inbox/<actor>/
   history.jsonl` files contain rows with `from.kind` /
   `payload.replyToId`. The new code's `readInboxHistorySince` parses
   these rows; consumers read `from.routingKind` / `payload.replyTo`
   and see `undefined`. **Decision (Claude reviewer concern):
   accept the risk + document the operator action.** Mitigation:
   - CHANGELOG v3.0.0 entry includes an explicit "Upgrade note:
     operators on mid-flight crews should run `/crews-leave-crew` or
     wipe `.crews/<crew>/inbox/` state before upgrading; stale
     on-disk inbox-history is not back-readable. CI's strict-mode
     gate guarantees no production code reads the legacy fields, so
     the impact is bounded to one-time stale-row visibility on a
     given crew's first review-mail after upgrade."
   - This matches the historical handling of every prior crews
     breaking change (v2.0.0 had no read-shim either, per CHANGELOG
     lines 244–253).
   - A consumer-side read-fallback shim was considered and rejected:
     it would dilute the schema-rejection invariant from US-001
     (the validator would have to tolerate the legacy names in the
     read path), reintroducing exactly the ambiguity v3.0.0 fixes.

6. **Marketplace version pin sync.** The toolkit-root
   `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` is pulled by every consumer via
   `copilot plugin update`. If only the per-plugin `plugin.json` is
   bumped, `gim-home` consumers may keep v2.4.1. Mitigation: US-006
   enumerates all 5 version files; the bookkeeper lead's standard
   post-merge step pushes toolkit `main` to ALL configured remotes
   (`origin`, `gim-home`, `personal` per codexu AGENTS.md bookkeeper
   invariants). This is process discipline, not implementation work.

7. **The `kindEnum` is shared between `env.kind` and the routing
   field.** Post-rename code uses the same enum, but the comment at
   line 40 of `envelope.js` ("kindEnum covers BOTH env.kind values AND
   from.kind routing values") must say "from.routingKind routing
   values" — a missed comment update would confuse future readers but
   not break runtime. Acceptance criterion AC-12 covers this.

8. **External impl-worktree placement (toolkit, not codexu).** Per
   codexu AGENTS.md cross-repo invariant, the impl worktree lives at
   `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/.worktrees/crews-protocol-v200-envelope-renames/`
   on branch `ralph/crews-protocol-v200-envelope-renames`, NOT
   anywhere under `D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/...` and NOT
   as a sibling-of-repo path. The lead merges the toolkit branch
   separately from any codexu changes (there are no expected codexu
   changes for this job — bookkeeper updates `data.json` after ship,
   in a separate commit).

## Preliminary Story Decomposition

Six stories within a single PR (atomic rename; no parallel-execution
win available — see Suggested Decomposition below).

- **US-001** — Schema rename + new explicit-rejection rules
  (`hooks/protocol/envelope.js` only; small surface; gates everything
  else; depends on AC-15 preflight).
- **US-002** — Producer chokepoint + direct payload setters
  (`hooks/mailbox.js` `appendSystemMailbox` lines 503–507 + 526;
  `hooks/stop.js:1085` `replyToId` payload-key rename).
- **US-003** — Non-test consumer rename
  (`hooks/protocol/review-required.js`,
  `hooks/commands/review-mail.js`,
  `hooks/stop.js:208–209` + `:265`).
- **US-004** — Test + fixture migration (producer-path matrix), ~33
  test files including the load-bearing
  `tests/protocol-envelope-enforcement.test.js` with positive +
  negative assertions per path.
- **US-005** — Validator strict-rejection tests (new unit-test bloc
  in `tests/protocol-envelope-canonical.test.js` or sibling).
- **US-006** — Docs + CHANGELOG + version bump (5 stamp files +
  `tests/version.test.js`'s `VERSION` literal + `docs/protocol.md`,
  `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `PLAN-1.0-crews.md`
  one-line top-note).

## Suggested Decomposition

All six stories share the same single-file chokepoint
(`hooks/protocol/envelope.js`) for the schema rules, and US-004 +
US-005 must observe BOTH the producer changes (US-002) AND the schema
changes (US-001) before tests pass. The only safe execution mode is
**serial within a single cluster**.

### Cluster: rename-bundle-serial
- Stories: US-001, US-002, US-003, US-004, US-005, US-006
- Phase: 1
- Depends on: None
- File-overlap evidence:
  - shared=`hooks/protocol/envelope.js` (US-001 edits, US-002/003/004/005
    read or reference; US-005 imports its exports)
  - exclusive(US-002)=`hooks/mailbox.js`, `hooks/stop.js` (payload literal)
  - exclusive(US-003)=`hooks/commands/review-mail.js`,
    `hooks/protocol/review-required.js`, `hooks/stop.js` (ack-gate reads)
  - exclusive(US-004)=`tests/**` (~33 files, including
    `tests/protocol-envelope-enforcement.test.js`)
  - exclusive(US-005)=`tests/protocol-envelope-canonical.test.js` (or
    sibling new file, implementer's choice)
  - exclusive(US-006)=`docs/protocol.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`,
    `CHANGELOG.md`, `PLAN-1.0-crews.md`, 5 version-stamp files,
    `tests/version.test.js` (US-002 also touches `hooks/stop.js`, but
    a different region — payload literal at line 1085 vs ack-gate
    reads at 208/265; the conflict is local and resolvable in a
    single commit).
  - risk=medium (atomic breaking change with high test-fixture sprawl;
    bounded by the new explicit-rejection schema rules and the
    enforcement matrix test).
- `execution_mode` rationale: Atomic breaking-change semver bump
  forbids partial intermediate states — every consumer must be on the
  new shape before strict-mode CI passes. Parallel sub-clusters would
  observe broken intermediate states (e.g., schema renamed but
  consumers still read old name, or producer renamed but tests still
  assert old name). Serial execution within a single worktree, single
  commit (or short stack of commits in a single PR), single
  fast-forward to main is the only safe shape.

Parallel handoff: `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/crews-protocol-v200-envelope-renames/plan.md --parallel --suggested-decomposition D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/crews-protocol-v200-envelope-renames/suggested-decomposition.json`

(Sidecar declares a single cluster — parallel mode degrades to serial.
Prefer the serial handoff: `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan
D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/crews-protocol-v200-envelope-renames/plan.md
--autonomous`.)
